intro: DOCX to HTML turns a Word document into a web page ready to open in any browser or to publish. It is practical for posting a text on an intranet, sending it as a page instead of a Word attachment, pasting it into a content management system or reading it on a device without Office.

The result is a single .html file: images go inside as data and formulas are written in MathML, which current browsers display without plug-ins. There are no folders or external resources that can get lost when you move it or send it by email.

The page is clean, semantic HTML, without the inline styles Word adds when saving as a web page: h1, h2 and h3 headings, paragraphs, lists, tables, links and footnotes at the end. It includes a simple, readable style sheet with automatic dark mode that you can replace with your own. Optionally, we add a table of contents with links to each section.
We convert with pandoc on our server, sandboxed and with no network access. You can upload up to 20 documents and, if there are several, also download a ZIP with all the pages.
steps: Say whether you want a table of contents at the top.
Download the HTML page or the ZIP with all of them.

faq.a: The structure and basic formatting are kept, not the layout: margins, page colours, text boxes and fonts are replaced by a clean web style.
Yes. It is readable HTML5 with a style sheet at the top; images are long data: attributes, but the rest of the text can be edited in any editor.

faq.q: What if I want to go back to Word?
faq.a: HTML to DOCX turns an HTML page into an editable Word document.
